data.narrative:
Proteus Space is a Series A aerospace & space company founded by David Kervin (CEO, 20+ years in US military contracting execution) and Andrew Shapiro (CTO, 20 years at NASA JPL, led 3D-printed component integration for Mars Perseverance Rover). The company has raised $14.4M to date. The valuation universe includes 5 public Space & Aerospace comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers across the sector.

Of three triangulation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using $17M as a proxy for enterprise value (derived from total capital raised) and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields $34M. Peer-median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-stage peer density within the Space & Aerospace sector (fewer than three same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables identified). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple (23.9x median across the five public tickers) could not proceed without disclosed revenue for the private target.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $29M–$39M, with a median point of $34M. This range reflects typical Series A step-up mechanics but carries material uncertainty given reliance on a single method. Key sensitivities include Proteus Space's near-term revenue trajectory relative to public-sector contracting pipeline milestones and technical validation against the broader competitive set (SpaceX, Sierra Space, Planet Labs, and similar private peers).
